title: Language Models Exhibit Inconsistent Biases Towards Algorithmic Agents and Human Experts

live_model.evidence: Sec 4.1 per-task scatter analysis: "gpt-4-turbo, rho=0.69, p<.01" (correlation with humans' per-task algorithm-aversion gap, Study 1, 27 tasks)

prompt.location: Appendix A ("Sample prompts and responses"), Appendix B ("An example prompt" for Study 2)

claim.metric: correlation (rho) between model's and humans' per-task algorithm-aversion gap
claim.location: Sec 4.1 scatter-plot analysis; 27 tasks from Table C.1 (Study 1, Castelo et al. task set), n=100 prompts per task

data.source: Task set adapted from Castelo et al. and Dietvorst et al. (Table C.1), including UCI Heart Disease and Student Performance datasets

notes: gpt-4-turbo's own mean trust-gap point estimate is plotted only in Figure 1 (star marker, not a printed number), so the correlation stat is used instead. Study 2 (algorithm-appreciation, n=200) reruns a 6-task subset; gpt-4-turbo did not consistently choose the more accurate agent there and produced most of the dataset's neutral/non-committal responses (94% of a 9.9% neutral total).
